segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer,
may not proceed to cross the highway,
who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1)
may continue to cross the highway
but must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone if one is provided or other place of safety before the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute'). The signal that indicates to a pedestrian is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faces: dev.position ('location of the device head') ahead of kin.position along kin.heading ('direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with no countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Entering the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) borrows (1)'s words: 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. It is the pedestrian's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto the roadway or lane r (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) made while the head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing r (dev.governs) showed walk and the pedestrian faced d (dev.position ahead of kin.position along kin.heading within the cone and reach).
Continuing to cross under this indication is the pedestrian's footprint still overlapping r (rel.occupies) at some observation while d shows the flashing indication without countdown.

Proceeding to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone or other place of safety is having left the roadway or lane crossed: the pedestrian's footprint no longer overlaps r (rel.occupies). Each place the words list (the curb's sidewalk, a safety zone, a median) lies off r. 'before the ... indication ... is illuminated and steady' fixes the moment: the observation at which d shows dont_walk_steady, having shown dont_walk_flashing without countdown at the previous one.

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (1)'s permission — the walk indication illuminated, the pedestrian facing the signal, proceeding across the highway in its direction — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (1)'s rule is a duty on drivers to give the right-of-way; whether that duty applied to some vehicle, held, or was complied with says nothing of how this pedestrian entered, so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. The judged observation is the onset of the steady indication of a pedestrian head d governing (dev.governs) a roadway or lane r: d shows dont_walk_steady here and showed dont_walk_flashing without countdown at the previous observation. The subject's latest step from a sidewalk onto r (history bound: that step, searched back without other limit) was made while d showed walk and the subject faced d; and the subject's footprint overlapped r at some observation since d last began showing dont_walk_flashing without countdown. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where that step lies before the recording, applicability is unknown.
obligation: At the onset of the steady indication the subject's footprint does not overlap r (rel.occupies): it has reached a place of safety off the roadway.

narrowings.why: 'a curb, sidewalk, safety zone ... or other place of safety' is read as any place off the roadway or lane the head governs; the kind of place reached is not checked.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps from the sidewalk onto r facing d while d shows walk; d turns dont_walk_flashing without countdown while it is mid-crossing, then dont_walk_steady while it is still on r.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but the pedestrian reaches the far sidewalk, off r, before d turns steady.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stepped onto r while d already showed dont_walk_flashing without countdown (no lawful entry under subparagraph (1)).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid but d's state is not observed.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the pedestrian already on r while d shows dont_walk_flashing without countdown; d turns steady while it is still on r; its step onto r is not recorded.
scenarios.boundary: the pedestrian's step from the sidewalk onto r, which lies before the recording

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a pedestrian signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08 (pedestrian signal heads placed at the far end of the crossing, in the pedestrian's line of sight)

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a pedestrian signal head at which the head counts as the one across the crossing the pedestrian faces: a wide urban crossing (six lanes and a median, about 30 m) plus the head's set-back behind the far curb
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08; AASHTO Green Book urban cross-section widths
